pass_1.locations: Original article Experimental Section pp. 4622–4623, extracted lines 75–137 and 169–185; original supplement p. S3, extracted lines 25–41
pass_1.finding: Read both originals after oligo scrape. The article describes coupling fatty-acid carboxyl to a 3′/5′ amino oligo on solid support, yielding an amide linkage, and sequential anchor/co-anchor labeling. Supplement lists the 20-base co-anchor AGTGACAGCTGGATCGTTAC and saturated C16–C24 fatty-acid choices. These establish inherited attachment chemistry; Hu Methods identifies the ZipSeq-specific strand and lipid choices. Independent second pass of Weber is still pending.

pass_2.locations: Weber et al. original PMC JATS Experimental Section “Synthesis of Lipid-Modified Oligonucleotides” extracted lines 101–164, Results/stepwise assembly lines 315–362; original supplementary PDF “Oligonucleotide Sequences” p. S3/extracted lines 25–43 and MALDI scope lines 52–65
pass_2.finding: Independently read both original article and its supplement after full ZipSeq source-bundle oligo scrape. Article specifies 5′/3′ amino-oligo solid-support synthesis and coupling of fatty-acid carboxyl to the free amine (amide bond), with sequential membrane insertion and co-anchor hybridization rather than a preannealed lipid duplex. Supplement gives the 20-base co-anchor AGTGACAGCTGGATCGTTAC with 3′ amino–C16/C18/C20/C22/C24 options and an anchor beginning GTAACGATCCAGCTGTCACT. MULTI-seq later selects 5′ lignoceric/C24 anchor plus 3′ palmitic/C16 co-anchor; Hu prints that choice and ZipSeq-specific extensions. Weber does not itself define the full ZipSeq barcode/caged oligo; no absence claim follows from this predecessor.
